data.name: Paramesh
data.gender_notes: Paramesh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Paramesh means 'supreme lord'. This name is derived from the Sanskrit words 'parama' meaning supreme and 'ish' meaning lord. In Hindu mythology, Paramesh represents the ultimate divine power and wisdom. The name Paramesh carries the meaning “Supreme Lord” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Paramesh usually hope their child will grow to embody supreme lord and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that evokes devotion and spiritual growth.
data.etymology: Paramesh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Supreme Lord.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Paramesh total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Paramesh highlights the profound reverence for the supreme deity in the Hindu culture, where the divine is believed to be the patron and protector of all beings. This name holds great respect and embodies the highest level of authority and power.
data.spiritual_significance: Paramesh holds deep spiritual significance as it is believed that calling upon the supreme lord or Paramatma brings peace, enlightenment, and the realization of one's true self. The name Paramesh reminds us of the eternal truth that the supreme lord is the source of all creation and remains in omnipotent and omnipresent form. The name also signifies surrendering one's ego and trusting in the divine's will and guidance, leading to inner peace and happiness.

vedic_reference.note: Paramesh is a name for the supreme god in Hinduism, often used interchangeably with Paramatma and Ishwar.

historical_references.reference: Parameshvara, a form of Shiva, is a popular deity in Hinduism. He is the lord of creation, preservation and destruction.
